lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: checking totals and fixing errors

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 4
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G4 Unit 3 — spending plans and comparison
objective: Learners recompute an invented total that was recorded wrongly, quantify the recording error, and re-test the corrected figure against the money available.
scenario: Isaac is an invented fourth grader checking a pretend supply order he wrote up: $21.75, $18.60, and $22.05. He recorded the total as $63.40 and has $65.00 of simulated money. The error in his record is what this task repairs.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Add Isaac's three invented amounts yourself before looking at his recorded total.

prompts.text: What is the correct total of Isaac's three amounts?

tasks.directions: Compare that with the $63.40 Isaac wrote down, then check the corrected total against his $65.00.

prompts.text: By how much is Isaac's recorded total wrong?
Using the correct total, how much of the $65.00 is left?

tasks.directions: Isaac adds a fourth invented item at $3.15 to the corrected order, not to his old recorded total.

prompts.text: What is the corrected total with the fourth item?
How far past his $65.00 does that put him?

tasks.directions: Had Isaac trusted his own record, he would have thought he had less room than he did.

prompts.text: Isaac's error made the order look more expensive than it was. Why is an error in that direction still worth fixing?

remediation: If a learner cannot locate the error, have them re-add Isaac's amounts in reverse order and compare the two runs step by step, so the disagreeing place value is isolated.
extension: Ask the learner to change one of Isaac's four amounts so the corrected order lands exactly on $65.00, and to show the arithmetic.
